The periodic table is a systematic arrangement of chemical elements, organized based on their atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties. It serves as a foundational tool in the field of chemistry, providing valuable information about the relationships between different elements.

Elements in the periodic table are grouped into rows called periods and columns known as groups or families. Elements within the same group typically share similar chemical characteristics due to their comparable electron configurations. The table is divided into various sections, including metals, nonmetals, and metalloids, each exhibiting distinct physical and chemical properties.
